text: Consider an LTI system with impulse response [latex]h(t)=e^{-5t}u(t)[/latex]. If the output of the system is [latex]y(t)=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t)[/latex] then the input, x(t), is given by
html: Consider an LTI system with impulse response [latex]h(t)=e^{-5t}u(t)[/latex]. If the output of the system is [latex]y(t)=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t)[/latex] then the input, x(t), is given by
subject: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
explanation_text: Impulse response of an LTI system = transfer function [latex]=\frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}=H(s)[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{where, } y(t)&=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; Y(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+3)}-\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \\ \text{Also, } h(t)&=e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; H(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ \text{Therefore, } X(s)&=\frac{Y(s)}{H(s)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \times (s+5) \\ &= \frac{2}{(s+3)}\\ \therefore \; \text{Input}&=x(t)=2e^{-3t}u(t) \end{aligned}[/latex]
explanation_html:
Impulse response of an LTI system = transfer function [latex]=\frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}=H(s)[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{where, } y(t)&=e^{-3t}u(t)-e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; Y(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+3)}-\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \\ \text{Also, } h(t)&=e^{-5t}u(t) \\ \therefore \; H(s) &=\frac{1}{(s+5)} \\ \text{Therefore, } X(s)&=\frac{Y(s)}{H(s)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+3)(s+5)} \times (s+5) \\ &= \frac{2}{(s+3)}\\ \therefore \; \text{Input}&=x(t)=2e^{-3t}u(t) \end{aligned}[/latex]

explanation_text: Given: [latex]\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x}_1\\ \dot{x}_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}u [/latex] or, [latex]\;\; \dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu [/latex] Here, [latex] [A]=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}, \;\;  B=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] State transition matric is given by, [latex]e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}[/latex] Now, [latex]  [sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 0 -1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]Adj[sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex] |sI-A|=(s-1)^2 [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; [sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{1}{|sI-A|}Adj[sI-A] [/latex] [latex][sI-A]^{-1}=\frac{1}{(s-1)^2}\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s-1} & \\ \frac{1}{(s-1)^2} & \frac{1}{s-1} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0\\ te^t& e^t \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex] \therefore[/latex]  State transition matrix[latex]=\begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0\\ te^t& e^t \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
explanation_html:
Given: [latex]\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x}_1\\ \dot{x}_2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 1&1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}u [/latex]
or, [latex]\;\; \dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu [/latex]

State transition matric is given by,
[latex]e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}[/latex]
Now, [latex] [sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 0 -1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]Adj[sI-A]=\begin{bmatrix} s-1 & \\ 1 & s-1 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
and [latex] |sI-A|=(s-1)^2 [/latex]

[latex] e^{\Delta t_1/RC}=2\;\;....(i) [/latex]

In time [latex] t=\Delta t_2 [/latex]
[latex]V_c=V_{LTP}; [/latex] [latex]V_{initial}=V_{UTP}; [/latex] [latex]V_{final}=-V_{sat} [/latex]
[latex]V_{LTP}=-V_{sat}+(V_{UTP}+V_{sat})e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]-\frac{V_{sat}}{2}=-V_{sat}+\left ( \frac{V_{sat}}{4}+V_{sat} \right )e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\left (1-\frac{1}{2} \right )V_{sat}=V_{sat}\left (1+ \frac{1}{4} \right )e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]\frac{1}{2}= \frac{5}{4}e^{-\Delta t_2/RC} [/latex]
[latex]e^{\Delta t_2/RC}=\frac{5}{2}\;\;....(ii)[/latex]
From equation (i) and (ii),
[latex]\frac{e^{\Delta t_1/RC}}{e^{\Delta t_2/RC}}[/latex]
[latex]=e^{(\Delta t_1-\Delta t_2)/RC}[/latex]
[latex]=\frac{2}{5/2}=\frac{4}{5}=0.8[/latex]
